approach.method_basis: The Parent grows molecular graph paths around two scored regional centers. Each region fits a count-fingerprint Gaussian process only to its own episode records, while a shared response amplitude scales the original correlated draws. The regions compete for evaluations by sampled scores. Purchased progress expands or contracts a region and can retire it and restart from an accepted molecule. Crossover also has access to the opposite accepted center, and the generated path records whether its final product is a direct noncopy recombinant. That donor support reaches purchases and later local learning, but direct products are systematically overpredicted on the observed purchased stream.
approach.novelty: Use the cumulative average of earlier direct-product prediction residuals as a common location offset for future direct products, frozen before each batch. The same offset shifts their predicted means and sampled scores, while all local fits, random residuals, donor support and progress rules remain. No same-Parent sibling has been evaluated. This tests a new consumer of observed source-specific errors, distinct from earlier donor expansion, shared-amplitude allocation and the historical pool-minimum location discount: it learns one signed offset from the actual prospective errors of this existing provenance class.

observed_bottleneck: The actual code Parent n-de8f05115faf pays for 261 direct noncopy recombinant products across the complete fifteen Search cells, yet has no decision consumer for their recorded prediction residuals. Its donor-access/feedback prediction activated, but its full/late utility conjunction was refuted: macro mean 0.5565416285347836 (SD 0.03252383969954171), paired loss 0.028072127962566307 to n-7d1e6230ecce, with all three seed macros lower. Direct products are overpredicted by 0.10293143 versus 0.03074638 elsewhere; their MSE is higher in 13/15 cells. The frozen search-policy audit, independently reproduced in policy/scratch/r0056-02-improve-L01/evidence-audit-summary.json and its audit-seed-<Search seed>-<task>.json files, keeps all 261 direct purchases, including 40 cold-start products: a batch-frozen cumulative residual mean reduces squared-error sum from 14.646438973992218 to 12.4845040670332 and improves 10/15 cells, with 221 products having earlier direct feedback. These audits cite the underlying nodes/n-de8f05115faf/seed-<Search seed>/logs/<task>.log and trajectories/<task>.jsonl files. This is a selected-stream feasibility diagnostic, not a measured adaptive score gain or identified cause of the Parent loss. The location-discount counterexample n-c415372c2c82 also shows why changing location alone must not be presumed to improve routing or score.

literature_review.conclusion: Reuse the frozen search-policy-r56-support-and-statistical-consumers review and its recorded queries, not a new search claim. Its reviewed RAVE, multivalid prediction and explicit mean-basis GP alternatives remain deferred; no borrowed algorithm element is adopted. GPML section 2.7 and the online-multivalid primary abstract were reopened to verify these boundaries: a coherent GP mean changes training centering, while formal multivalidity requires its own online algorithm. This plan only offsets the existing direct-class decision location from earlier paid base residuals, preserving local fits and donor support. The prior chronological replay motivates a falsifiable prospective-error test; conversion and formal-Anchor performance must be measured independently.
literature_review.internal_evidence_reason: The exact new consumer is justified by n-de8f05115faf accepted direct-product provenance and prospective errors, the source-verified batch-frozen residual audit (261 paid direct products; squared-error sum 14.646438973992218 to 12.4845040670332; 40 cold-start products retained), and the inherited local/shared-amplitude separation in n-7d1e6230ecce. The negative routing precedent n-c415372c2c82 prevents assuming location modification is beneficial. The estimator is an internal fixed heuristic; none of the reviewed external algorithms is introduced, and the selected-stream audit does not identify population calibration or an adaptive score counterfactual.

hypothesis: Introduce exactly one session-wide prequential direct-provenance decision-location offset. Let D_t contain all unique earlier accepted optimizer products in the current Objective Session whose recorded path.cross_origin.direct_noncopy_terminal is true and whose original uncorrected emission-time GP mean m_i is finite. Before announcing batch t, set b_t = sum_{i in D_t}(y_i-m_i)/|D_t|, or exactly 0 when D_t is empty. Freeze b_t for the entire batch. For every direct-class candidate j, use corrected mean m_j+b_t and active sampled score s_kj+b_t; non-direct candidates retain m_j and s_kj exactly. The coefficient is one, with no floor, clipping, decay, window choice, warmup threshold or coefficient fitting. The estimator uses base residuals only, pools qualifying accepted receipts from both regions and survives regional retirement, but resets at the next Objective Session. Local GP conditioning membership, covariance, amplitude, normal draws, graph construction and controller are unchanged. This is a source-conditioned decision-location heuristic, not a coherent new GP posterior, population-bias estimator, uncertainty correction or multivalid algorithm.

finding_summary.headline: Direct-product error correction worked and improved the code Parent mean, while formal-Anchor performance remained below target
finding_summary.insights:
The registered intervention settles a limited but useful question: earlier errors from an existing provenance class can change real decisions and reduce prospective error on the resulting paid stream without changing the local Gaussian processes. This is a substantive new error consumer, not another donor expansion or numerical retune, and it adopts none of the deferred literature algorithms. It leaves the Parent donor-support result intact. The complete matched panel supports a positive mean total effect of this particular consumer on its code Parent, but does not identify error reduction as the cause of the score gain or establish transferable calibration. Direct purchases fell from 261 to 144, and their own incumbent-improvement mass fell from 0.17186 to 0.14211 even as total progress rose; most realized gain therefore came through the rest of the evolving search, not more useful direct products. Late corrected direct-product MSE remained 0.07619 versus 0.01765 for nondirect purchases, so a single provenance offset did not resolve the conditional prediction problem. A candidate-dependent ranking or predictive model is the relevant kind of method for that remaining distinction; this result supplies no justification for tuning the scalar estimator.

The trajectories also show that better local prediction did not fix molecular routing. Fragment-excluded within-batch similarity increased from 0.7250 to 0.7418, reaching 0.7627 late, while the count above fifty heavy atoms rose from 153 to 448. The Molecular assessment found broad overall scaffold diversity but only 7-26 generic scaffolds in each task upper-score cohort, plus repeated enlargement, unusual heteroatom bonds and absent stereochemical assignments. This supports a limitation in finding coherent alternative whole frameworks, rather than a lack of graph novelty. Scaffold-preserving reconnection proposals and chemically credible attachment choices are the kind of capability that could address it; their benefit is untested here. The remaining Anchor gap, variable cell effects, missing trusted safety verdict and unmeasured alternative histories keep broader performance and mediation questions open. This node does not decide the fate of the regional approach.
finding_summary.results: All fifteen sessions completed. Nonzero offsets reached 8,638 direct recombinant candidate occurrences and changed the purchased set in 56 of 435 batches, replacing 99 paid identities. On the 144 direct products actually purchased, mean squared prediction error fell from 0.0246044 to 0.0230033; all 40 cold-start products stayed in that comparison. The improvement was heterogeneous: six task/seed cells improved, five worsened and four stayed unchanged. The local-model and sampling laws stayed intact, and independent reconstruction matched all 870 Child fit and draw blocks. Full incumbent improvement mass rose from 5.22074 to 5.35395, and late mass rose from 0.63777 to 0.84245, each measured over the complete paid denominator. Mean final score rose from 0.556542 to 0.565422, a paired gain of 0.008880; two seed macros fell slightly and the third rose by 0.033875. The formal Anchor remained higher at 0.607030, so its +0.002 performance target was not reached. There was no technical failure.

molecular.headline: Aromatic polycycles and amine/carbonyl frameworks remain diverse, with enlarged graphs, unusual heteroatom bonds and unassigned stereochemistry.
molecular.overall_character: Assessed all supplied Search trajectories for n-85bacee96fb3 and actual code Parent n-de8f05115faf: seeds 0/1/2, all five tasks, Research in Depth profile epoch 1, 300 accepted observations per cell including ten initial observations. Child evaluation and Parent pairing are both complete; no supplied trajectory is missing. The structural aggregates exclude initial molecules and cover 4,350 accepted optimizer outputs per node; unpurchased candidate fields and rejected proposals are not represented. Child molecules span 1-120 heavy atoms, with median 30; Parent spans 1-110 with median 29. Ring-closure text rates are 0.9494-0.9701 and aromatic-text rates 0.9092-0.969 across tasks, consistent with abundant aromatic and fused/bridged ring chemistry. These are molecule-level text frequencies, not aromatic atom fractions. The Child has 2,121 nonempty typed and 1,392 generic Murcko scaffolds versus Parent 2,038 and 1,300: graph diversity is broad, while individual high-score families are much narrower. Ordinary amines, amides, carbonyl heterocycles and ethers coexist with N-halogen/O-halogen bonds, unusual bridges, polyenes and very small cleavage products. The moderate drug-likeness judgment describes recognizable medicinal motifs, not measured developability. No synthesis, conformational feasibility, stability, potency or stereochemical benefit is established. Read-only RDKit descriptors and same-task molecule/score associations support the chemistry below; they do not attribute a contribution to the algorithm intervention. Evidence and definitions: policy/scratch/r0056-02-improve-L01-molecular/molecular-audit-summary.json; policy/scratch/r0056-02-improve-L01-molecular/trajectory-provenance.json; policy/scratch/r0056-02-improve-L01-molecular/evidence-index.json. The provenance file preserves each original Child staging path and the SHA-256 of its byte-identical run-local snapshot, plus the authoritative published Parent paths. No historical panel or formal Anchor chemistry is substituted for this actual-Parent comparison.

per_task.generated_character: The 870 accepted outputs are mostly compact carbonyl-bearing aromatic systems: median 24 heavy atoms, three perceived rings and two aromatic rings. Seed 0 favors methoxy-substituted indene carboxamides with N-N substitution and aryl thiols; seed 1 retains an indole-like carboxamide family; seed 2 forms a more bridged pyridyl/aminomethyl framework with a ketone and an N-O-containing ring. Parent median size is also 24, with related carbonyl/aromatic chemistry; the seed-2 leading molecule is shared. These are recognizable functional groups in increasingly unusual connectivity. Evidence: policy/scratch/r0056-02-improve-L01-molecular/audit-seed-0-zaleplon_mpo.json; policy/scratch/r0056-02-improve-L01-molecular/audit-seed-1-zaleplon_mpo.json; policy/scratch/r0056-02-improve-L01-molecular/audit-seed-2-zaleplon_mpo.json.
liabilities: N-N-substituted amides, N-O ring bonds, thiols and strained-looking bridges warrant chemical scrutiny; favorable labels do not verify their stability or synthesis.
The output includes 32 molecules below six heavy atoms, which lack the complete architecture present in the stronger examples.
missing_features: Reliable retention of the compact connected carbonyl/aromatic arrangement during scaffold edits is missing from the weak cleavage and ring-opening products.
Explicit configuration is absent where the bridged and substituted rings create potential stereogenic centers; the score evidence does not specify a preferred stereoisomer.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial indole carboxamide scores 0.3051048084. The Child seed-2 ketone/aminomethyl/thiol structure scores 0.4597940971; its counterpart without the thiol scores 0.4583866383, so thiol addition is not established as the driver. The final seed-2 variant with an opened peripheral aromatic arrangement scores 0.1310986923, while methane scores zero. Compact, intact carbonyl/aromatic arrangements associate with the better observations; neither maximum size nor any particular new heteroatom bond is sufficient.

per_task.generated_character: This is the large-molecule tail: median 49 heavy atoms, eight perceived rings and five aromatic rings, versus Parent medians 40, six and four. Of 870 outputs, 415 exceed fifty heavy atoms, versus 122 in Parent. Seed 0 produces repeated carbonyl-rich aza-heterocycles joined by long unsaturated branches; its leading graph has 106 heavy atoms. Seed 1 has an ester/aryl/imine-rich leading structure with 53. Seed 2 instead favors a 40-heavy-atom polyheteroaromatic dicarbonyl block, arylamino linkage and bridged acetal; that leading molecule is also present in Parent. Ring abundance here does not imply a feasible three-dimensional scaffold. Evidence: policy/scratch/r0056-02-improve-L01-molecular/audit-seed-0-deco_hop.json; policy/scratch/r0056-02-improve-L01-molecular/audit-seed-1-deco_hop.json; policy/scratch/r0056-02-improve-L01-molecular/audit-seed-2-deco_hop.json.
liabilities: Long polyene/imine branches, chloromethyl substituents and repeated aza-carbonyl blocks make several graphs difficult to regard as ordinary medicinal compounds.

The upper-score cohort includes 46 graphs with an RDKit ring of at most four atoms whose atoms are all aromatic; this connectivity flag warrants geometry review and is not proof of an independently aromatic small ring.
missing_features: The output lacks consistent size-controlled access to complete alternative frameworks: repetitive expansion is common even though the stronger observed family is more compact.
Stereochemically and geometrically resolved alternatives to densely bridged acetal/ring junctions are not demonstrated.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The seed-2 40-heavy-atom structure scores 0.6271061188, whereas the much larger seed-0 and seed-1 leaders score 0.5995651179 and 0.6097170170. Dichloromethane scores 0.5. The upper 87 observations occupy 33-42 heavy atoms and only seven generic scaffolds. The observed gradient favors particular connected heteroaromatic arrangements over fragments and repetitive enlargement; it does not demonstrate that more rings or more atoms are independently beneficial.

per_task.generated_character: The 870 outputs have median 32 heavy atoms, five perceived rings and two aromatic rings; Parent median size is also 32. High-score chemistry includes flexible tertiary amines linking fluorinated aminoaryl groups to fused carbocycles, an N-aryl azetidine, and more rigid bridged amine cages. Primary amines and potentially basic tertiary centers are clearly present, so a missing-basic-amine diagnosis would be incorrect. Seed 1 retains the Parent leading amine/thiol/halogenated-ring structure; seed 2 shifts from the Parent amine/sulfinamide framework toward a compact bridged aza-polycycle. Evidence: policy/scratch/r0056-02-improve-L01-molecular/audit-seed-0-drd2_docking.json; policy/scratch/r0056-02-improve-L01-molecular/audit-seed-1-drd2_docking.json; policy/scratch/r0056-02-improve-L01-molecular/audit-seed-2-drd2_docking.json.
liabilities: O-F, occasional S-F and N-N additions appear around otherwise plausible amine frameworks; their labels establish no chemical stability.
Azetidines and bridged amines can be legitimate motifs, but the particular cage junctions and unassigned stereochemistry require structural assessment.
missing_features: Consistently conventional bond environments around otherwise useful amine/aromatic arrangements are missing from part of the high-scoring output.
Defined stereochemical identities are absent despite potential tetrahedral centers in 836 of the 870 outputs; neither the trajectories nor their labels establish a preferred configuration.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The seed-0 29-heavy-atom tertiary-amine structure bearing an O-F group scores 0.9999944950; an analogous amino/phenol/azetidine structure without O-F scores 0.9955038762. Seed 1 and seed 2 leaders score 0.9785347864 and 0.9926636180. An early oxygen-rich cyclic-acetal/aryl-sulfone structure scores 0.0004099201. Better observations combine substantial ring surfaces with accessible amine centers, but the close high-scoring conventional example prevents interpreting O-F as a necessary chemistry feature.

per_task.generated_character: The 870 outputs have median 34 heavy atoms, five perceived rings and two aromatic rings, versus Parent medians 32, five and three. Leading molecules connect aryl or aza-aryl surfaces through large heteroatom-containing rings or bridged frameworks, with N-methyl cyclic amide/imide groups and ether/amine linkages. Seed 1 has a large diaryl heterocycle linked to a cyclic dicarbonyl diamine; seed 2 retains an aza-aromatic substituent on an ether-linked polycyclic lactam. Parent leaders also combine aza-aromatics and cyclic carbonyl/nitrogen groups, but their connectivity differs. Evidence: policy/scratch/r0056-02-improve-L01-molecular/audit-seed-0-median_2.json; policy/scratch/r0056-02-improve-L01-molecular/audit-seed-1-median_2.json; policy/scratch/r0056-02-improve-L01-molecular/audit-seed-2-median_2.json.
liabilities: The best graphs have complex macrocyclic or bridged connectivity and multiple potential stereocenters without assignments; synthetic accessibility is uncertain.
Thirty outputs have fewer than six heavy atoms and 21 exceed fifty, so size changes sometimes discard or overextend the complete framework.
missing_features: More reliable access to alternative coherent arrangements of aromatic surfaces and cyclic carbonyl/nitrogen groups is missing; broad graph novelty alone does not show this capability.
Configuration and feasible conformations are unresolved for the large rings and bridged junctions.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aromatic dicarbonyl heterocycle scores 0.1678386595. Child seed leaders score 0.2236540869, 0.2289244791 and 0.2223506670, all at 35 heavy atoms. Acetylene scores zero. The upper 87 observations occupy 32-39 heavy atoms and generally retain both aromatic surfaces and carbonyl/nitrogen-bearing rings; the lower cohort includes fragments and larger disrupted graphs. These observations support preservation of a distributed functional arrangement, not an inferred unseen target scaffold.

per_task.generated_character: The 870 outputs center on 27 heavy atoms and carbonyl-rich nitrogen heterocycles, often with fluorinated small carbocycles and aryl or conjugated-chain substituents. Median aromatic-ring count is three versus Parent one. Seed 0 produces a fluorinated cyclobutene attached to a fused imino/carbonyl nitrogen framework; seed 1 combines a difluorocyclopropyl group, a fused aza-dicarbonyl system and an amino-polyene chain; seed 2 uses an indane-like aryl group and a cyclic imine substituent. N-halogen connectivity occurs in 451 outputs versus Parent 183. The seed-1 leading molecule is shared with Parent. Evidence: policy/scratch/r0056-02-improve-L01-molecular/audit-seed-0-sitagliptin_mpo.json; policy/scratch/r0056-02-improve-L01-molecular/audit-seed-1-sitagliptin_mpo.json; policy/scratch/r0056-02-improve-L01-molecular/audit-seed-2-sitagliptin_mpo.json.
liabilities: Multiple N-F bonds, an amino-polyene segment with unspecified alkene geometry, and highly fused or unsaturated small-ring frameworks make chemical stability and synthesis questionable.
Forty-five outputs have fewer than six heavy atoms. Ring and aromatic text coverage remain high overall, so the limitation is not absence of ring generation.
missing_features: Stable-looking, conventionally connected alternatives to the heavily N-fluorinated carbonyl frameworks are poorly demonstrated among the leading observations.

Reliable preservation of the full substituent arrangement and explicit stereochemistry is absent during edits; both tiny fragments and larger concatenations miss the favorable observed size/architecture balance.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Seed leaders score 0.5937642989, 0.6565392185 and 0.4216706564, whereas a much larger concatenated aromatic/aza-dicarbonyl structure scores 1.2904215119e-57. The upper 87 observations have 24-30 heavy atoms; 82 contain an N-halogen bond. Yet the final seed-1 molecule still has N-F bonds and scores only 0.0020528874. The data associate a particular size and functional arrangement with higher labels, not N-F alone; neither those bonds nor a required replacement pharmacophore can be justified from the score.

N-halogen-bearing outputs number 569 versus 326 and O-halogen-bearing outputs 150 versus 126. High labels coexist with such connectivity, while other highly labeled amine/aromatic molecules lack it. This is chemistry association, not evidence that these bonds cause improvement or that any algorithm component causes their incidence. transferable_gaps.gap: Conventional attachment chemistry is not reliably retained while useful amine, carbonyl and aromatic arrangements are elaborated.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator needs the capacity to vary attachment positions, polar groups and size using conventional bond environments as well as the unusual environments already reached. Useful alternatives must be learned from current-session feedback; these observations supply neither a universal exclusion list nor an established intervention benefit.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
